correctness.rationale: The exact conditional increment law follows by inspecting the trailing-one run of an integer. Splitting \(n=2^kq+a\) isolates all high-block and cross-boundary effects. The valuation classes \(j=\nu_2(a)\) give the complete and disjoint low-word census, including the \(j=k-2\) and \(j=k-1\) boundary exceptions. The four class sums \(W_0=W_1=37/8\) and \(W_j=8-27/2^{j+2}\) for \(j\ge2\) follow from explicit conditional survival formulas. Their exact geometric sum gives \(T_k=83\cdot 2^{k-6}\), hence \(P_k=83/128\) for every \(k\ge4\); finite direct substitution gives \(k=1,2,3\). Conditional tail probability decays geometrically, ensuring genuine natural densities. The included verifier checks all key formulas with exact rationals plus finite independent integer instances. No computational enumeration is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a direct, exact infinite-family answer to the open adjacent-one analogue of the Cusick comparison inequality. Shifts \(2^k-1\) have only one one-block regardless of size, so existing many-block normal approximations do not resolve their bias. The unexpected finite-length stabilization at \(83/128\) is a quantitative structural law, with a carry-class proof showing the cancellation that causes it. No larger conjecture is asserted.
